Convert continuous trait values into the states of a discretized trait

Source: R/convert_values_to_states.R
convert_values_to_states.Rd

Assigns each trait value to a state, using the same cut points and states as a simmap obtained with phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap(). This is typically used to convert the continuous trait values of the missing taxa as states of the simmap used to constrain the grafting, e.g., to fill the allowed_states of the taxa.

A tolerance can be applied to the values to account for their uncertainty, or for the uncertainty of the cut points: each value is then assigned to all the states covered by the interval [value - tolerance, value + tolerance].

Usage

convert_values_to_states(
  values,
  simmap = NULL,
  breaks = NULL,
  states = NULL,
  tolerance = 0
)

Arguments

values

Numeric vector. The trait values to convert, in the same units as the trait used to build the simmap. If named, the names are kept in the output (e.g., the names of the missing taxa). NA values give NA states.

simmap

A "simmap" or "multiSimmap" produced by phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap(), which carries the cut points and the names of the states in its attributes "breaks" and "states". Alternatively, leave it as NULL and provide breaks and states (e.g., for a simmap built from tip values binned by yourself).

breaks

Numeric vector. Only used if simmap = NULL. The interior cut points between the states, in increasing order and different from each other.

states

Character vector. Only used if simmap = NULL. The names of the states, from the lowest to the highest values. Must have one more element than breaks, because N interior cuts (breaks) produce N+1 groups.

tolerance

Numeric, zero or positive. Default is 0: each value is assigned to a single state. With a tolerance, each value is assigned to all the states covered by the interval [value - tolerance, value + tolerance], in the units of the trait. Values that are farther than tolerance from every cut point are still assigned to a single state. It can be a single number used for all the values, or a vector with one tolerance per value (e.g., the measurement error of each missing taxon). See 'Details' for more information.

Value

A list of character vectors, with one element per value, named as in values (unnamed if values is not named). Each element contains the states of the value, ordered from the lowest to the highest values: a single state by default, and several states for the values close to a cut point if a tolerance is used. The state of a NA value is NA.

The output can be used directly as the allowed_states item of a list of missing taxa, if values is named after the taxa. To get a simple character vector with a single state per value, e.g., to compare the states of tips or nodes, use unlist() (only when tolerance = 0, as the elements have then one state each. With a tolerance, the elements can have several states).

Details

Each state covers the values from its lower cut point (included) up to its upper cut point (excluded): a value equal to a cut point belongs to the state above it. The first and last states are open-ended, so values below the first cut point or above the last one are assigned to the lowest and highest states.

Tolerance

By default (tolerance = 0), each value is assigned to a unique state. To include uncertainty, tolerance assigns several states to the values that are close to a cut point, as accepted by allowed_states in the grafting functions: a value gets the state of value - tolerance, the state of value + tolerance, and all the states in between. The same rule applies at the edges of the interval as for the values: if value + tolerance is equal to a cut point, the state above this cut point is included (and if value - tolerance is equal to a cut point, the state above it is the first state of the value). A tolerance makes the constraint of the grafting weaker: the taxa can be grafted on a wider set of branches (see phylograftR::check_grafting_plan() to evaluate how much, with the valid_fraction).

See also

Other functions from phylograftR:

  • phylograftR::convert_contMap_to_simmap() to obtain the simmap and its cut points from a continuous trait map (contMap).

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_taxa() to graft taxa based on target clades and excluded subclades, using the states to constrain the grafting.

  • phylograftR::graft_missing_clades() to graft groups of missing taxa as sister clades, using the states to constrain the grafting.

Author

Maël Doré

Examples

# Load backbone phylogeny
data(toy_backbone)

# Simulate a continuous trait on the backbone and interpolate it with phytools::contMap()
tip_data <- phytools::fastBM(toy_backbone, a = 0, sig2 = 1)
my_contMap <- phytools::contMap(tree = toy_backbone, x = tip_data, plot = FALSE)

# Discretize the trait into three states using quantiles
my_simmap <- convert_contMap_to_simmap(my_contMap, probs = c(1/3, 2/3),
                                       states = c("low", "medium", "high"))
# Inspect the trait values used as breaks
attr(my_simmap, "breaks")
#> [1] 2.039502 3.502385

# Define continuous trait values of three missing taxa
missing_values <- c(Taxon_1 = -2, Taxon_2 = 0.1, Taxon_3 = 3)
# Convert continuous values into the same states used in the converted simmap
# The output is a list with the states of each value
my_states <- convert_values_to_states(missing_values, simmap = my_simmap)
my_states
#> $Taxon_1
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_2
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_3
#> [1] "medium"
#> 

# To get a character vector with a single state per value, use unlist() (if tolerance = 0)
unlist(my_states)
#>  Taxon_1  Taxon_2  Taxon_3 
#>    "low"    "low" "medium" 

# Same conversion with the cut points and states given directly
convert_values_to_states(missing_values, breaks = attr(my_simmap, "breaks"),
                         states = c("low", "medium", "high"))
#> $Taxon_1
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_2
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_3
#> [1] "medium"
#> 

# --- Account for the uncertainty of the values with a tolerance --- #

# Taxon_2 has a value just above the second cut point, between the states "medium" and "high"
close_values <- c(Taxon_1 = -2, Taxon_2 = attr(my_simmap, "breaks")[2] + 0.1, Taxon_3 = 3)
convert_values_to_states(close_values, simmap = my_simmap)
#> $Taxon_1
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_2
#> [1] "high"
#> 
#> $Taxon_3
#> [1] "medium"
#> 

# With a tolerance of 0.3 trait units, values close to a cut point get several states
allowed_states <- convert_values_to_states(close_values, simmap = my_simmap, tolerance = 0.3)
allowed_states
#> $Taxon_1
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_2
#> [1] "medium" "high"  
#> 
#> $Taxon_3
#> [1] "medium"
#> 

# One tolerance per taxon, e.g., the measurement error of each value
# (no tolerance for Taxon_1 and Taxon_3)
convert_values_to_states(close_values, simmap = my_simmap, tolerance = c(0, 0.3, 0))
#> $Taxon_1
#> [1] "low"
#> 
#> $Taxon_2
#> [1] "medium" "high"  
#> 
#> $Taxon_3
#> [1] "medium"
#> 

# The output can be used directly as the 'allowed_states' of a list of missing taxa
missing_taxa_list <- list(Taxon_name = names(close_values),
                          Target_clade = list(Taxon_1 = "t1",
                                              Taxon_2 = c("t1", "t2"),
                                              Taxon_3 = "t1"))
missing_taxa_list$allowed_states <- allowed_states
